task: Horizon 12 of the agent-agnostic-browser-bridge project (tools/chrome-bridge/). Change the existing `findElement` page action so that instead of returning only a match count it returns the matched elements themselves: a stable element ref (a self-contained CSS-locator string re-consumable by the same findElement/clickElement surface), the element's visible innerText, and a fixed key-attribute map (tagName plus id, class, role, aria-label, href, name, type, data-testid). It must stay a pure ISOLATED-world chrome.scripting DOM read (CSP-safe, no caller-supplied string eval), target the dedicated sandbox tab like every other page action, add no new manifest permission, and cap result size (max match count + per-element innerText length) applied in-page before the structured-clone boundary. Then live-verify in a fresh post-rebuild chrome-bridge MCP session with a Chrome head-to-head against claude-in-chrome's find. Resolves package blocker #6. Follows the established change-one-atomic-page-action-across-the-parity-surface then live-Chrome verification pattern used by horizons 7-11.

analysis.objective: Deliver horizon 12's slice of the agent-agnostic browser bridge vision by upgrading the existing `findElement` page action from an existence check into an extraction tool that returns the matched elements themselves (stable ref + visible innerText + a fixed key-attribute set), across the full parity surface, closed by a live-Chrome head-to-head.
analysis.successDefinition: `findElement` returns, for a given CSS selector against the dedicated sandbox tab, an ordered list of matched elements — each carrying a stable element ref, the element's innerText, and the fixed key-attribute map (tagName plus id, class, role, aria-label, href, name, type, data-testid, absent keys null per package convention) — with the element list capped like the other read actions (documented cap constant, truncated/total fields), the pre-existing found/matches summary deliberately superseded; the implementation is a single pure ISOLATED-world chrome.scripting.executeScript function-ref DOM read (no chrome.debugger/CDP, no caller-supplied string eval, selector reaches querySelectorAll only as a serialized argument, adversarial selector string cannot execute); the change lands atomically across FindElementParams/FindElementResult in protocol/types.ts plus both mapped Record<PageAction,…> types, the raw + guarded handlers in page-actions.ts, the TOOL_CATALOG entry with an honest updated schema, the three unit test files (both PAGE_ACTIONS count assertions still pass at 20, new shape asserted, adversarial-selector test added), and the README (prose, enumeration, manual-e2e step); git diff of manifest.json vs HEAD is empty and built dist permissions are unchanged; the reliably-green subset of npm run verify is green; and a mandatory live-Chrome head-to-head in a fresh post-rebuild chrome-bridge MCP session shows findElement returning real refs+text+attributes for a real page selector, an empty list (not an error) for a no-match selector, the cap enforced on a high-cardinality selector, and the adversarial selector producing no code execution — compared against the equivalent claude-in-chrome find; on success tools/chrome-bridge/blockers.md item #6 is marked resolved and the roadmap memory files are updated.
assumptions: The element ref is a self-contained CSS-locator string the same findElement/clickElement surface could later consume (a generated selector, e.g. an :nth-of-type chain or the caller selector plus an index token), not a live object handle or a CDP backend node id — a persistent CDP session is explicitly out of scope for this slice.
innerText (visible, layout-aware text) is returned, truncated per-element to a documented per-element char cap, distinct from the whole-list result cap.
The key-attribute set is exactly the task's list (id, class, role, aria-label, href, name, type, data-testid) plus tagName, with no caller-configurable attribute selection this horizon.
Nullable/absent fields follow the package convention (T | null, never undefined; exactOptionalPropertyTypes respected).
The result cap mirrors an existing read action's pattern (a MAX_* constant + truncated boolean and a total-match count), reusing the existing truncate helper per-element where it fits.
The h9/h11 'stale MCP catalog — new/changed tool not callable in-session' symptom may recur and is cleared by a --retry in a genuinely fresh post-rebuild MCP session, not by code changes.

executeScript in the ISOLATED-world read is ports.executeScript (chrome.scripting, function ref, ISOLATED world by omission) as already used by getPageText/readPage/waitFor — not the MAIN-world executeScript page action.
Live verification is done through Claude Code only (decision 2026-09-03 h4); Gemini/Codex/Cursor remain documentation-only.
risks: Changing FindElementResult shape while keeping the findElement action name is a breaking protocol change; if any consumer or test depends on the old {found, matches} contract the atomic-diff discipline must catch every site or tsc/tests break.

ref design: an index-based ref is unstable across DOM mutation between calls; a generated-selector ref can be non-unique or huge on obfuscated-class pages (the LinkedIn _96169ba5 case from blocker #5) — the chosen scheme must be defensible without over-engineering.

The unfocused sandbox tab's suspended render pass (h10) can make innerText return collapsed/empty values or a mid-hydration snapshot; verification page choice must account for this and the tool must not silently imply the text is complete.
innerText on many matched nodes plus attributes can blow past result size on real pages; the cap must be enforced in-page before serialization, not after.
In-session MCP catalog staleness (h9, h11) can force the horizon to end MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING before a --retry clears it — expected, but blocks a same-session green close.
class attribute values can be very long on framework pages; not truncating them defeats the size cap, truncating them can break a class-based ref.

Getting innerText (not textContent) depends on the node being rendered; ISOLATED-world executeScript reads layout — confirm it returns visible-text semantics in the unfocused sandbox tab, not a textContent fallback.
outOfScope: Network response bodies for text/JSON (blocker #4) — a separate capture-layer slice; horizon 12 ships exactly one capability.
clickElement by text/role or a fuller pointer-event sequence (blocker #5) — separate deferred slice, even though obfuscated-class pages motivate both.
Reviving the horizon-05 DOM page-model / bounding-box snapshot — a different, larger capability that findElement-returns-elements deliberately does not become.
Full-page / element screenshots, captureTab({fullPage}) (blocker #7) — unrelated deferred slice.
Trusted CDP Input.dispatch* input and any persistent/multi-call CDP session — contraindicated (h10) until a rendering/focused-tab story exists; this slice stays pure chrome.scripting.
Deleting the dead active-tab surface (queryActiveTab/ActiveTab/captureVisibleTab/redundant activeTab permission) — only folded in if given its own horizon; not bundled here.
Making findElement accept text/XPath/role locators as input — this horizon changes the output shape only; the input stays a single CSS selector string.
Caller-configurable attribute lists or a fields parameter — the key-attribute set is fixed this horizon.
Adding any new manifest permission or switching the CDP session model — explicitly forbidden by the task.
Wiring tools/chrome-bridge/ into the repo-root build or migrating boky onto it (binding decision 2026-09-02 h1).
analysis.domainShapeReason: The work is a protocol/adapter change inside a single extraction subsystem — one page action, its typed parity surface, an ISOLATED-world DOM read, and a live-Chrome verification — with no business rules or domain model involved.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: One entry in PAGE_ACTIONS (protocol/actions.ts), the single source of truth; findElement is an existing one being changed, not added.

The set of sites that must change together for one action: Params/Result interfaces + both Record<PageAction,…> mapped types, raw + guarded handlers in page-actions.ts, TOOL_CATALOG schema, the unit test files, and the README.
The dedicated, deliberately-unfocused Chrome tab that is the sole target of every page action (decision h6); its render pass is suspended while unfocused.
A ports.executeScript call with a function reference running in the content-script isolated world — CSP-safe, no string eval, selector passed only as a serialized argument.
The stable per-match CSS-locator string findElement returns for each matched element so it can be re-targeted later, without holding a live handle or CDP node id.
The fixed map returned per matched element: tagName plus id, class, role, aria-label, href, name, type, data-testid.
The documented size limit (max element count and per-element innerText length, with a truncated flag) applied in-page before serialization, mirroring the other read actions.
The mandatory horizon-closing check: run the changed action in a fresh post-rebuild chrome-bridge MCP session and compare its output against claude-in-chrome's equivalent find on the same real page.

discoveryFindings.area: unfocused sandbox tab — innerText vs textContent
discoveryFindings.finding: The sandbox tab is deliberately unfocused (sandboxTabActive:false) and its render pass is suspended while unfocused (README:87-89, :264-266; h10). h10's live check on a Wikipedia page still got meaningful scrollHeight/scrollY; h09 got real innerText from document.querySelector('h1')?.innerText via evaluatePage (CDP, not chrome.scripting). Current getPageText uses document.body.innerText; readPage uses outerHTML. No code comment warns innerText collapses to empty in the unfocused tab; the analysis flags it as a risk to verify, not established fact.

The live head-to-head must specifically check the returned text is non-empty/non-collapsed on the chosen verification page. h09/h10 evidence suggests layout reads work in the sandbox tab but were via CDP evaluatePage — ISOLATED chrome.scripting innerText needs empirical confirmation in the live-verify phase. phases.name: Return matched elements from the findElement action
phases.goal: Change the existing findElement page action so that, for a CSS selector against the sandbox tab, it returns an ordered capped list of matched-element descriptors — each with a self-contained CSS-locator element ref, the element's visible innerText, and the fixed key-attribute map — wired atomically across the whole parity surface with unit tests.
phases.rationale: Today findElement only answers 'how many elements match' with {found, matches}. An AI coding tool driving the browser needs the elements themselves — a re-usable locator, the text they show, and their identifying attributes — so it can act on a specific match. This phase does that as a pure isolated-world DOM read (a chrome.scripting call whose injected function runs in the content-script isolated world, so it is not blocked by a site's Content-Security-Policy and never evaluates caller-supplied strings), with the payload size bounded inside the page before it crosses the serialization boundary.
changes: Add MAX_FIND_ELEMENT_MATCHES (element-count cap) and MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS (per-element innerText cap) constants in page-actions.ts next to DEFAULT_MAX_CHARS.

Rewrite the raw.findElement injected isolated-world function (ports.executeScript(tabId, fn, [selector]), no options arg) to slice the NodeList to the element-count cap, build a per-match descriptor with a self-contained CSS-locator ref string (size-bounded, re-consumable by the findElement/clickElement selector input), a capped visible innerText, and the fixed key-attribute map (tagName plus id, class, role, aria-label, href, name, type, data-testid; absent keys as null), and return an ordered array plus total match count and a truncated flag — all bounded before the structured-clone boundary; keep the try/catch that makes a hostile selector return an empty result.

Replace FindElementResult in protocol/types.ts with { readonly matches: readonly FindElementMatch[]; readonly total: number; readonly truncated: boolean } and add adjacent FindElementMatch and key-attribute-map interfaces with nullable fields typed T | null (never undefined); the two Record<PageAction,…> mapped types reference by name and need no edit.

Add coerceFindElementOutcome(raw) mirroring coercePointerOutcome: guard Array.isArray, rebuild every descriptor from primitives (asString/null-coerce each attribute, asString the ref and text), return { result: { matches: [], total: 0, truncated: false } } for a real empty match, and a CSP error sentinel for a malformed/empty injection return.
Update the findElement TOOL_CATALOG entry description to state it returns the matched elements (ref, innerText, key attributes) with the result cap; leave inputSchema unchanged.

Rewrite the three existing findElement unit tests to the new result shape (keeping the executeScript toHaveBeenCalledWith(7, expect.any(Function), ['.x']) / queryActiveTab-not-called assertions), add an injected-function test that extracts the fn and runs it against a stubbed document, and add the repo's first adversarial-selector test proving the hostile string reaches querySelectorAll only as a serialized argument and yields an empty list.

Update README read-actions prose to describe the new findElement output and its cap, and add a new numbered manual-e2e step (real selector -> refs+text+attributes; no-match -> empty list not error; high-cardinality selector -> cap enforced; adversarial selector -> no execution); keep the 'twenty'/'20' page-action counts unchanged.

existing raw.findElement handler and coercePointerOutcome pattern in page-actions.ts
clickAt/hover injected-function unit-test pattern in page-actions.unit.test.ts
the fixed key-attribute set and cap model from the task analysis
phases.expectedResult: findElement returns an ordered, size-capped list of matched-element descriptors (element ref + visible innerText + fixed key-attribute map) across the full parity surface, with the reliably-green subset of npm run verify passing and PAGE_ACTIONS still 20 entries.

rubric.label: CSP-safe ISOLATED-world extraction, no string eval
rubric.ruleStatement: The rewritten raw.findElement must run as a function reference via ports.executeScript in the content-script isolated world, with the selector passed only as a serialized argument — never interpolated into code, never through string eval / new Function / CDP Runtime.evaluate with an expression string.
passCriteria: raw.findElement is passed to executeScript as a function value (func/reference form), not a template string
The CSS selector reaches the injected function exclusively via the args array; the injected body shows no ${selector} / string concatenation into a query
No eval(, new Function(, Runtime.evaluate-with-expression, or <script> injection anywhere on the new path
The injected function references only DOM globals available in the isolated world and closes over no page-world symbols
failureExamples: A careful dev builds document.querySelectorAll(' + selector + ') inside a stringified injected function to 'avoid an extra arg' — works in manual testing, is a CSP/no-string-eval violation
Selector is correctly passed as an arg but the descriptor's innerText is gathered via a second executeScript that evals el.outerHTML parsing
Injected function calls a helper defined outside its own body, so it throws ReferenceError once actually serialized and injected

rubric.label: Result cap enforced in-page before the structured-clone boundary
rubric.ruleStatement: MAX_FIND_ELEMENT_MATCHES and MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS must be applied inside the injected function — the NodeList sliced and each innerText truncated before the array is returned across the structured-clone boundary — and total must reflect the pre-slice count with truncated set accordingly.
passCriteria: Both constants are defined once and referenced by the injected function (inlined into its body is acceptable; a shared import that survives serialization is not)
Slicing happens before descriptor construction: the function never builds more than the cap's worth of descriptors
total = full match count before slicing; truncated = (total > cap) OR any innerText was cut
Per-element innerText is sliced to MAX_ELEMENT_TEXT_CHARS in-page, not by the guarded handler after return
A selector matching >cap nodes returns exactly cap matches, correct total, truncated:true
failureExamples: Dev maps the full NodeList to descriptors, then does .slice(0, MAX) on the returned array in coerceFindElementOutcome — cap works but a 5000-node match already serialized 5000 innerText strings across the boundary
truncated is set only for the match-count overflow and stays false when innerText was truncated but count was under the cap
total is computed as matches.length after the slice, so it can never exceed the cap and the flag is meaningless

rubric.label: Element ref is a re-usable self-contained CSS locator
rubric.ruleStatement: Each match's ref must be a plain CSS selector string that, re-fed to findElement or any querySelector against the same document, resolves to that same element — carrying no live handle, CDP node id, XPath, or index into a prior result set.
passCriteria: ref is typed and returned as string and is a valid CSS selector (parses; uses >, nth-of-type, #id, attribute selectors — not /html/body/... XPath)
Given a document with duplicate-looking siblings, each returned ref selects exactly one node and they differ between matches
ref contains no serialized DOM node, no numeric CDP/backend node id, no opaque token that only the current injection can resolve
The injected-function unit test asserts that feeding a returned ref back through the same query yields the original element
When an element has a stable unique id, ref prefers #id over a long structural path
failureExamples: Dev returns ref as `${selector}:nth-of-type(${i})` where i is the loop index — breaks whenever the original selector already had a combinator or matched across parents, so the ref re-resolves to the wrong node or nothing
ref is built from element.className split on spaces joined with . — producing an invalid selector for elements with dynamic/space-containing class tokens
Path is correct but anchored at the matched element with no root context (div.item), matching 40 nodes on re-query instead of the one

rubric.label: Full parity surface migrated atomically, proven by tsc
rubric.ruleStatement: The new Result shape must be threaded through every parity-surface file in one coherent change such that tsc --noEmit and the reliably-green verify subset pass, PAGE_ACTIONS still has 20 entries, and no FindElementResult-era field or type name survives.
passCriteria: FindElementResult replaced by { matches: readonly FindElementMatch[]; total: number; truncated: boolean }; FindElementMatch + key-attr interface are adjacent and exported as needed
Both Record<PageAction, …> mapped types (Params + Result) still compile exhaustively; raw and guarded handler entries both updated
TOOL_CATALOG findElement description updated to describe extraction; inputSchema byte-identical to before
README read-actions prose updated and a new numbered manual-e2e step added; every existing 'twenty'/'20' count unchanged
pnpm typecheck + pnpm lint + unit tests green; grep for FindElementResult and old existence-check field names returns zero hits outside git history
failureExamples: Dev updates the interfaces, handlers, and tests but forgets the second mapped type (Result Record<PageAction,…>), and because the old entry was structurally similar tsc only errors in one spot they patch with a cast — lint's no-as rule then fails the build
README prose is updated but the manual-e2e step is not added, or an unrelated 'twenty' in the count sentence gets rewritten to 'twenty-one'
inputSchema is 'tidied' (property reordered / description added) so downstream schema-snapshot test drifts

rubric.label: Nullable-field convention + adversarial-selector / malformed-injection handling
rubric.ruleStatement: Absent key attributes must be null (never undefined, never omitted), the field types must read T | null, and coerceFindElementOutcome must rebuild descriptors from primitives — returning the empty outcome for a legitimately-empty match and the CSP error sentinel for malformed/empty injection output, with a hostile selector yielding empty (not a throw).
passCriteria: Every key-attribute interface field is declared string | null; the injected function emits explicit null for missing attrs (verified against a stub-document element lacking those attrs)
exactOptionalPropertyTypes is on, so an accidental ?: or x: undefined would fail tsc — and it compiles, proving the convention held
coerceFindElementOutcome guards Array.isArray, reconstructs each descriptor field-by-field from primitives (no pass-through of the raw object), and does not trust raw shape
Empty match -> {matches:[],total:0,truncated:false}; undefined / non-array / shape-mismatch injection result -> the same CSP error sentinel used by coercePointerOutcome
New adversarial-selector test feeds an invalid/hostile selector (e.g. >>> / unbalanced [ / script-like payload) and asserts empty result via the injected function's try/catch, no exception propagated
failureExamples: Dev returns the descriptor object directly from the injected function and coerceFindElementOutcome just does Array.isArray(raw) ? raw : [] — a poisoned/partial entry (missing ref, innerText a number) flows straight to the caller
Missing attributes are emitted by spreading el.getAttribute(name) ?? undefined into the map, so keys are undefined rather than null and slip past tsc but violate the stated convention

Adversarial-selector test asserts the guarded handler catches the throw, rather than the injected function's own try/catch returning empty in-page — so a real hostile selector still surfaces a console error in the sandbox tab

phases.healerHint: If a dimension fails, fix it inside the injected ISOLATED-world function and the coercion guard rather than in the guarded handler — the cap, the null-normalization, the ref construction, and the hostile-selector try/catch must all live before the structured-clone boundary, and every parity-surface file (both mapped types included) moves in the same commit so tsc proves completeness.

phases.name: Verify findElement elements live in Chrome head-to-head
phases.goal: In a fresh post-rebuild chrome-bridge MCP session, run the changed findElement against a real page, compare its output to claude-in-chrome's find, confirm no manifest permission changed, and mark package blocker #6 resolved.
phases.rationale: A real-Chrome end-to-end check closes any horizon that changes the extension, because unit tests cannot prove the isolated-world DOM read returns real refs and non-collapsed visible text from the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab (a tab kept in the background whose browser render pass is suspended). This phase runs that check and records the result; it stays blocked until it can be run in a genuinely fresh MCP session after rebuilding the extension.
changes: Rebuild and reload the extension, open a fresh chrome-bridge MCP session (use --retry if the tool catalog is stale from a prior session).

Run findElement on a real-page CSS selector and confirm real element refs, non-empty non-collapsed innerText, and a populated key-attribute map; run a no-match selector and confirm an empty matches list (not an error); run a high-cardinality selector and confirm the element-count cap and truncated flag; run the adversarial selector string and confirm no code execution.
Run claude-in-chrome's find on the same page and record the head-to-head comparison of the two results.
Confirm git -C tools/chrome-bridge diff HEAD -- extension/manifest.json is empty and diff extension/manifest.json dist/extension/manifest.json stays identical.
Append a dated 'Verified 2026-09-04 (horizon 12)' head-to-head block to the README, mark blockers.md item #6 resolved, and update the roadmap state/discoveries memory files.
inputs: Phase 0 deliverable (changed findElement across the parity surface)
blockers.md item #6 and the h11 manifest-diff verification method
phases.expectedResult: A dated 'Verified 2026-09-04 (horizon 12)' head-to-head block in the README with blockers.md item #6 marked resolved; the phase ends blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING until executed in a fresh post-rebuild chrome-bridge MCP session.
phases.compensation: Revert the README verification block and the blockers.md #6 status change if the live head-to-head fails or cannot be run.

rubric.label: Fresh post-rebuild MCP session is evidenced, not asserted
rubric.ruleStatement: The recorded evidence must demonstrate that the head-to-head ran in a genuinely fresh chrome-bridge MCP session started AFTER the rebuild+reload, or must honestly end the phase blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING.
passCriteria: README block names the rebuild/reload step and shows a concrete freshness signal (new session id, --retry note if catalog was stale, a ping/getTabState round-trip timestamp, or tool-catalog hash) tying the session to the post-rebuild build
The findElement output quoted shows the NEW extraction shape (ref + innerText + key-attribute map), proving the running extension is the rebuilt one

If a fresh session could not be obtained, status is recorded as blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING with the reason, and the README/blockers changes are withheld or marked provisional per the compensation
failureExamples: README says 'ran in a fresh session after rebuilding' with no session id, no ping, no catalog signal — ordering asserted only
Executor rebuilt but the quoted findElement output still shows the old return shape (bare found/matches), indicating a stale service worker was hit
Phase marked passed while the narrative admits the MCP catalog still showed the old findElement signature

rubric.label: Every findElement branch hit live with quoted output
rubric.ruleStatement: The README block must show real quoted output for all four required scenarios: normal match, no-match, high-cardinality cap, and adversarial selector string.
passCriteria: Normal-match case: quoted output shows >=1 real element ref, non-empty innerText that is not collapsed/whitespace-only, and a populated key-attribute map
No-match selector: quoted output is an empty matches list with a success status, explicitly NOT an error/throw
High-cardinality selector: quoted output shows the element-count cap enforced AND truncated:true AND per-element innerText length capped
Adversarial selector string: quoted output shows it was treated as a locator string with no code execution and no internal error leak
Each scenario names the real page/URL it was run against
failureExamples: Executor exercises normal + no-match live but describes the cap and adversarial cases from the unit tests / code reading rather than live output
truncated flag never appears in any quoted output; reviewer cannot confirm the in-page result cap fired
Adversarial case run but only 'no error occurred' is stated — the actual returned payload is not quoted
innerText shown is the collapsed empty string and executor does not flag it

rubric.label: claude-in-chrome find corroborates on the same page
rubric.ruleStatement: claude-in-chrome's find must be run on the identical real page and its result compared field-by-field against findElement, with divergences explained.
passCriteria: README block quotes claude-in-chrome find output for the same URL and same target as at least the normal-match findElement case
A concrete comparison is recorded: which elements both tools found, whether refs/locators point at the same nodes, whether innerText and attribute data agree
Any divergence (different match count, ordering, ref format, text normalization) is listed and explained rather than glossed
Conclusion states whether findElement's extraction output is at parity with or better than claude-in-chrome find for the extraction use case
failureExamples: Both tools run but the write-up only says 'results matched' with no quoted claude-in-chrome output
claude-in-chrome find run on a different page or selector than findElement, making the comparison non-parallel
findElement returns 3 matches, claude-in-chrome returns 5, and the block does not address the gap
Comparison covers only presence/absence of elements, never the innerText or key-attribute payload that is the point of this upgrade

rubric.label: Manifest unchanged, shown by real before/after diffs
rubric.ruleStatement: The evidence must include the actual output of both required git/file diffs proving no manifest permission changed and the built manifest matches source.
passCriteria: Quoted output (or explicit 'empty, no output' with the exact command) for git -C tools/chrome-bridge diff HEAD -- extension/manifest.json
Quoted result for the source-vs-dist comparison of extension/manifest.json against dist/extension/manifest.json showing they are identical
Both commands are shown as actually run (command line + result), not merely claimed
If any diff is non-empty, the phase does not claim pass on this dimension
failureExamples: README states 'confirmed manifest unchanged' with no command output shown
Only the git diff is shown; the source-vs-dist manifest comparison is skipped
dist/ was not rebuilt so the source-vs-dist check trivially passes against a stale artifact, and this is not noted
Diff shown but it is git diff (unstaged only) when manifest changes were already staged

rubric.label: Deliverable edits and status recording are honest and complete
rubric.ruleStatement: The README verification block, blockers.md #6, and the roadmap memory files must be updated consistently with the evidence, with no self-grading and status matching what was actually demonstrated.
passCriteria: README contains a block dated exactly 'Verified 2026-09-04 (horizon 12)' with the head-to-head evidence inline
blockers.md #6 is marked resolved with a pointer to that README block, OR left open if the live check did not fully pass
roadmap state.md and discoveries.md are updated to reflect the outcome (including any stale-catalog / --retry discovery, consistent with the h9/h11 pattern)
Status is one of passed / blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING and matches the evidence; no numeric self-score is asserted; claims are backed by quoted output not paraphrase
If compensation was triggered, the README block and blockers.md #6 change are reverted and that is recorded
failureExamples: blockers.md #6 flipped to resolved but the README block only covers the normal-match case — cap and adversarial paths never verified
README block present and dated but state.md / discoveries.md left untouched
Executor writes 'verification scored 9/10' or similar self-grading
Phase recorded as passed while the narrative admits the cap case is 'expected to work based on the unit test'
Stale-catalog retry happened but is not captured in discoveries.md

phases.healerHint: If a dimension is thin, run the missing branch live in a genuinely fresh post-rebuild chrome-bridge session and paste the real tool output (findElement and claude-in-chrome find) plus both manifest diff commands into the dated README block; if a fresh session is genuinely unavailable, record the phase as blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING and revert the README/blockers edits rather than asserting a pass.

successCriteria: findElement returns, for a CSS selector against the sandbox tab, an ordered list of matched elements each carrying a stable CSS-locator ref, visible innerText, and the fixed key-attribute map (tagName plus id, class, role, aria-label, href, name, type, data-testid; absent keys null), capped in-page with total + truncated fields.

The implementation is a single pure ISOLATED-world chrome.scripting.executeScript function-ref DOM read — no chrome.debugger/CDP, no caller-supplied string eval, selector reaches querySelectorAll only as a serialized argument, and an adversarial selector cannot execute code.

The change lands atomically across the parity surface (FindElementParams/FindElementResult + both mapped Record types, raw + guarded handlers, TOOL_CATALOG description, the edited findElement unit tests plus the two count-assertion test files still passing at 20 and a new adversarial-selector test, the README) with the reliably-green subset of npm run verify passing.
No new manifest permission: git diff of extension/manifest.json vs HEAD is empty and the built dist manifest permissions are unchanged.

Return matched elements from the findElement action: findElement returns an ordered, size-capped list of matched-element descriptors (element ref + visible innerText + fixed key-attribute map) across the full parity surface, with the reliably-green subset of npm run verify passing and PAGE_ACTIONS still 20 entries.

Verify findElement elements live in Chrome head-to-head: a dated 'Verified 2026-09-04 (horizon 12)' head-to-head block in the README with blockers.md item #6 marked resolved; the phase ends blocked MANUAL_CHROME_CHECK_PENDING until executed in a fresh post-rebuild chrome-bridge MCP session.
deferred: Network response bodies for text/JSON (blocker #4) — a separate capture-layer slice; horizon 12 ships exactly one capability.
clickElement by text/role or a fuller pointer-event sequence (blocker #5) — separate deferred slice, even though obfuscated-class pages motivate both.
Reviving the horizon-05 DOM page-model / bounding-box snapshot — a different, larger capability that findElement-returns-elements deliberately does not become.
Full-page / element screenshots, captureTab({fullPage}) (blocker #7) — unrelated deferred slice.
Trusted CDP Input.dispatch* input and any persistent/multi-call CDP session — contraindicated (h10) until a rendering/focused-tab story exists; this slice stays pure chrome.scripting.
Deleting the dead active-tab surface (queryActiveTab/ActiveTab/captureVisibleTab/redundant activeTab permission) — only folded in if given its own horizon; not bundled here.
Making findElement accept text/XPath/role locators as input — this horizon changes the output shape only; the input stays a single CSS selector string.
Caller-configurable attribute lists or a fields parameter — the key-attribute set is fixed this horizon.
Adding any new manifest permission or switching the CDP session model — explicitly forbidden by the task.
Wiring tools/chrome-bridge/ into the repo-root build or migrating boky onto it (binding decision 2026-09-02 h1).
A caller-supplied fields/attributes parameter for findElement — fails YAGNI gate 1 (asked for): no current consumer needs configurable attribute selection.

A dedicated clickElement path that consumes the new element ref directly — fails YAGNI gate 3 (speculative abstraction): the ref is already a plain CSS-locator string the existing clickElement input accepts.
A persistent / multi-call CDP session or backend-node-id element handles — fails YAGNI gate 3 and is contraindicated (h10).
